_: The deployed DogTag system on ROAX. One set. Every address here was deployed by contracts/script/Deploy.s.sol in a single run, and every contract in contracts/src is represented exactly once. This file describes what is running, not how it came to be.
_roles: admin is the protocol authority: it owns ProviderRegistry (Ownable2Step) and holds DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on DogTagSBTConsent, VerificationRegistryConsent and ProtocolRegistry, plus PUBLISHER_ROLE on the last. It is also the key that must broadcast Deploy.s.sol, because the registrar wiring in that script is onlyOwner on a core the script has just handed to it.
_custodian: The SBT's immutable neutral custodian. Every dog tag is minted here and never to an owner's wallet, so ownerOf carries no owner meaning and can never be compared as identity. It must have no code, hold no role anywhere, and never sign - it is a sink, not an actor.
_frozen_verifier: Groth16VerifierConsent is redeployed rather than reused, and its runtime bytecode is byte-identical to the previously deployed frozen-ceremony verifier - compared directly with cast code against the superseded instance 0x868B0B57... after this broadcast, equal string for string and 1933 bytes in both. Equal LENGTH is necessary but not sufficient, which is why the comparison is over the bytes. So the on-chain VK is unchanged and NO zero-knowledge artifact rotated: the consent circuit, its ceremony, consent_final.zkey (sha256 f83a111f...), consent.graph and both mobile bundles are untouched by this deployment. Changing any of them would be a ceremony decision, not a deployment one.
_root_index: VerificationRegistryConsent.rootIndex is the DogTagIssuerFactory. It is immutable, so the factory named here is the one this registry resolves every anchored root through for its whole life - replacing the factory means replacing the registry too, and repointing every client. That is the deliberate price of the pointer not being rewritable by anyone.
_publication: PUBLISHED. dogtag-levelb/1 is live and active on both axes with its binding, executed 2026-08-04 on THIS ProtocolRegistry by PublishProtocolVersions.s.sol (propose at blocks 339355-339357, execute at 339359-339361, publisher 0x8E27E117... which holds PUBLISHER_ROLE == keccak256("PUBLISHER") - read off the deployed contract, not recomputed from the variable name). getDiscoverySet(keccak256("dogtag-levelb/1")) returns a 9-word record decoded and compared member-for-member against this file: factory, verificationRegistry, sbt, verifier and providerRegistry each equal to the key above, circuitId == keccak256("consent.circom/DogTagConsent(6)"), active == 1. getActiveArtifactSet resolves; minAppVersion 1.4.0. The four artifact pins were not transcribed - they agree three ways: sha256 of the committed circuits/build files, the LEVEL_B_V1 descriptor in crates/dogtag-prover-rs/src/artifact.rs, and the record the superseded registry was already carrying. Note the getter is getDiscoverySet - getContractSet belongs to an earlier record shape and is absent here, and calling it reverts at the dispatcher with EMPTY returndata, which reads identically to an unpublished version. Before publication getDiscoverySet reverts with the contract's own named "unknown discovery set"; that is the honest pre-publication state, not a deploy failure.
_deployment: 2026-08-04, ROAX chain 135. All nine contracts deployed by one run of contracts/script/Deploy.s.sol, broadcast by admin 0x8E27E117... at blocks 339337-339348 (12 transactions: 9 CREATEs then the 3 onlyOwner registrar-wiring calls). This REPLACES the 2026-08-03 set in full. WHY ALL NINE: PRs #143 and #144 changed DogTagIssuer and #143 changed ProviderRegistry - measured, not inferred, by comparing the compiled runtimes against cast code on the previous instances (DogTagIssuer 4022 -> 4739 bytes, ProviderRegistry 20975 -> 21187). Those two cascade through every immutable that pins them: DogTagIssuerFactory pins both implementation and registry, VerificationRegistryConsent pins providerRegistry and rootIndex (the factory), ProviderDirectory pins core, ServiceDomainResolver pins core and factory. That is six forced. The remaining three - the SBT, the frozen verifier and the discovery registry - move because Deploy.s.sol deploys a COMPLETE, INDEPENDENT set by design and cannot partially replace a running one. VERIFIED: every receipt status 0x1; the whole sequence was rehearsed first on an anvil fork of ROAX (deploy, publish, a full provider journey and the pillar) and produced identical addresses; and _assertWiring re-read every immutable from the deployed contracts inside the same broadcast, so a constructor-argument mistake would have failed the deploy.
_provisioning: Deployed, wired and PROVEN END TO END, then left with the walk's own provider in place. The 2026-08-04 verification walk registered one provider (providerId 0x12f607346023b299410b735818cd5a3321ecf77b, controller 0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266 - the well-known public anvil account 0, chosen so anyone can act as it on a disposable testnet) and drove the full registrar sequence to canIssue == true, twice: a VACCINATION clone 0xdD1533D621fFba833738267B6b3ff58b71605d57 and a TRAVEL_CLEARANCE clone 0x0Ca65d55D9092Cac03A1981Afd9a115905A526E3. THE SEQUENCE HAS TWO STEPS THAT ARE INVISIBLE FROM A PLAN AND LEAVE THE RECORD INERT IF MISSED: registerProvider writes standing PENDING, so setProviderStanding(ACTIVE) is required; and attachService likewise writes service standing PENDING, so setServiceStanding(ACTIVE) is required. A THIRD is not a step at all: confirmServiceOwner reverts NoChange() on a fresh attach, because attachService already wrote confirmedOwner = liveOwner and ownerEpoch = 1 - it exists for a LATER owner handover. The anvil rehearsal is what established that, and it would otherwise have been discovered against the live chain. Finally canIssue stays FALSE until the PROVIDER's own repointService lands, while canRevoke and isRecognizedIssuer are already true - that asymmetry is the nested ladder folding the current-service pointer, not a fault. canCreateService must be asked AS THE FACTORY (cast call --from <factory>): with no from, msg.sender is zero, no generation matches, and it answers false for every provider on earth. Registering further providers remains a registrar KYC decision - drive it from the admin portal's registrar surface.
_sbt_rotation_ruling: CAPTAIN RULING 2026-08-03: KEEP this fresh DogTagSBTConsent. Settled - do not re-litigate, and do not 'restore' the previous SBT as a compatibility measure. WHAT ROTATING COST: this SBT holds no profileRoot for any previously minted tag, so every credential issued before this deployment stops verifying, and a dogTagId the old SBT had permanently retired (mintCustodial refuses an id whose root is already set, and that refusal survives a burn) is mintable again here. WHY IT WAS RULED RIGHT ANYWAY: reusing the old SBT would have preserved NOTHING. Verification needs BOTH R == profileRoot(dogTagId) AND rootIndex.rootIssuer(R) != 0, and rootIndex moved to the new factory, which has never seen a historical root - so every pre-existing credential answers 'unknown root' whichever SBT is in the slot. The old profileRoots would have been preserved into a state where they could not verify. Testnet state is disposable by standing ruling. WHY THIS IS NOT THE ZK CONSTRAINT: the must-not-rotate rule exists so no zero-knowledge artifact needs regenerating, and the SBT appears nowhere in the circuit or the VK. Nothing ZK rotated - see _frozen_verifier. Rotating the VERIFIER would be a ceremony decision and remains captain-gated; this was not that.
_protocol_registry_redeploy: This ProtocolRegistry carries PUBLISH_TIMELOCK 0, per the captain's 2026-08-03 ruling that testnet waits not at all and production keeps 2 days. The floor lives in the deploy script (Deploy.validatePublishTimelock), which refuses anything but DEFAULT_PUBLISH_TIMELOCK (172800) unless TESTNET_DEPLOY=true is stated aloud - this deployment stated it. Production is expressed by that default plus the opt-in and NEVER by inspecting block.chainid: ROAX 135 is itself a live chain, so a require(block.chainid == 135) guard passed on exactly the deployment it claimed to refuse. Redeploying the registry is routine rather than unfixable, because a mobile rebuild+reinstall accompanies every full redeploy as standing process.
_verification_walk: What was PROVEN on this set on 2026-08-04, on chain rather than by compiling. (1) THE ANCHOR: getDiscoverySet decoded to nine words matching this file member for member, active. (2) THE PROVIDER JOURNEY: reached canIssue(clone, signer) == true, live. (3) THE TWO-LAYER ISSUANCE CHECK, both halves. PR #143's closure - a signer holding the scope-free authority bit (core.canIssue true) who is NOT on a clone's own list (clone.issuanceAllowed false) is REFUSED by that clone: issue() reverts 0xa649bcb3, confirmed with cast sig to be NotLocallyAllowed(). PR #144's seed - a freshly deployed clone already carries issuanceAllowed[creator] == true, so the provider can anchor through the contract it just deployed. (4) THE MANDATORY ISSUER-WHITELIST PILLAR, end to end on the surface where a wrong address renders a genuine credential as "this credential is forged": a real TRAVEL_CLEARANCE was issued and anchored (root 0x06adf0807e3a7c3b060180642d4a871013b0f19f836fb5c47483340bcd7ae19c, tx 0x4176f05a9b19813a78f5d01d92be83df4a290cf5b6f049db181b82179697571d) by a government-api running LIVE against these addresses, and its UNAUTHENTICATED POST /v1/verify answered verdict true with issuerWhitelisted true and issuerWhitelistState "passed". THE GREEN WAS SHOWN TO MEAN SOMETHING: pointing that same verifier's FACTORY_ADDR at the superseded factory, changing nothing else, made the SAME credential come back verdict false with the pillar unresolved and rootIssuerRead "noRecord" - and reverting restored true. At the chain level the pillar's own reads were replicated independently: rootIssuer(R) -> clone, clone.registry() -> the governing authority (this ProviderRegistry, NOT a client's configured one), the RootIssued log for the anchoring (blockNumber, logIndex), and the address-keyed RightsSet history folded at that point with the ISSUE bit masked out of the word rather than the word compared whole. RightsSet topic0 is 0xbc9c679fe541a4f3fcf5f2887c4adcd6e7703f7ea9d0933b8862662f8290af7f.
_clients: REPOINTED, and repointing was a re-run rather than a hunt, because addresses are configuration read from this file BY KEY NAME. scripts/gen-deployment-env.sh projects it onto every stack's variable names (admin, vet, groomer, government, indexer and the four web surfaces) and scripts/gen-mobile-roax-config.sh writes the two gitignored mobile bundles; both were re-run and every projection resolves the keys above. make check-addresses passes, and it is BIDIRECTIONAL - an undeclared file carrying a ledger or retired address fails, AND a declared file that no longer carries one fails too - with the superseded set derived from this file's own git history rather than hand-curated, so it could not go stale by being forgotten. WHAT A REGENERATED MOBILE BUNDLE IS NOT: editing apps/*/roax.json is not a repoint. Those are COMPILE-TIME, so nothing changes on a handset until the app is rebuilt AND reinstalled - the captain's standing per-redeploy process, and a step this deployment has NOT performed.
